google/gemini-2.5-flash.mistake: The logical implication `p_13(Brianna) → ¬p_10(Brianna)` ('If Brianna is open-minded, then she is not skeptical') might incorrectly represent the relationship between open-mindedness and skepticism. While they aren't directly synonymous, open-mindedness doesn't necessitate a lack of skepticism. A person can be open to new ideas (open-minded) and still critically evaluate them (skeptical). The FOL asserts a stronger, potentially exclusionary relationship that isn't inherently present in the common understanding of these terms.
